explanation: Heating zinc carbonate strongly in limited air converts it to zinc oxide, releasing carbon dioxide — calcination, the carbonate-ore equivalent of roasting a sulphide ore.

beaker_view.final_appearance: A similar-looking white residue of zinc oxide.

thermal.visual_cue: Needs strong, sustained heating to decompose at all.

beaker_view.observation: Heated strongly, the pale powder gives off carbon dioxide — the colour barely changes, but the mass does as the gas escapes.
